bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar govt sets target of AI training for 5 lakh students in five years - The Hans India
bihar_raw_news.content: Home News National News Bihar govt sets target of AI training for 5 lakh students in five years In Short Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary chaired a review meeting on the proposed Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 at Sankalp Hall in Lok Sevak Awas on Thursday, where officials discussed measures to promote AI-based innovation, attract investment and generate employment opportunities in the state. IANS Created On: 22 Oct 2026 8:34 PM IST Comment Share : X Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Patna: The Bihar government has set a target of providing Artificial Intelligence (AI) training to five lakh students over the next five years to enhance their employability and prepare them for emerging technological demands. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary chaired a review meeting on the proposed Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 at Sankalp Hall in Lok Sevak Awas on Thursday, where officials discussed measures to promote AI-based innovation, attract investment and generate employment opportunities in the state. During the meeting, Choudhary stressed the need to create a conducive environment for AI companies, startups and digital enterprises to establish and expand their operations in Bihar. The initiative aims to develop the state as a hub for emerging technologies and digital innovation while opening new avenues of employment for young people. The Bihar government is also exploring incentives to encourage investment in the development of advanced AI technologies, including large-scale AI models. Officials discussed the need to strengthen the technical infrastructure required to support the sector and promote state-led initiatives to accelerate its growth. Choudhary directed the concerned department to constitute a dedicated team to oversee the implementation of the policy and ensure that its targets are achieved within a stipulated timeframe. As part of the initiative, the state government plans to organise a major AI-focused event in Bihar every year for the next five years. The events will bring together technology experts, companies, startups and students to facilitate knowledge-sharing, collaboration and innovation. The proposed Bihar Artificial Intelligence Policy 2026 seeks to promote technological advancement, skill development and digital entrepreneurship while attracting private investment to the state. The initiative assumes significance as Bihar seeks to expand employment opportunities for its large young population and address concerns over unemployment. By equipping students with AI-related skills, the Bihar government aims to improve their access to emerging job opportunities and encourage them to pursue technology-based entrepreneurial ventures. The policy is expected to focus on building the state's AI ecosystem through industry participation, improved infrastructure and targeted training programmes. The state government aims to use these measures to strengthen Bihar's digital economy and create new opportunities for its youth over the coming five years. bihar_raw_news.title: India's data centre boom lifts IT investments - ET Datacenters
bihar_raw_news.content: Investments & Deals 1 min Read India's data centre boom lifts IT investments India's information technology (IT) services sector saw investments rise to 4.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) between Q42025 and Q32026. This increase, driven by new data centre projects, represents a significant jump from 0.8 per cent a year prior. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 22, 2026 at 07:41 AM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights IT services investments reached 4.5 per cent of GDP in Q42025-Q32026, up from 0.8 per cent. Data centre projects and revised costs drove 28.4 per cent of new investment announcements. Union Budget 2026-27 tax holiday for foreign firms boosted investment announcements. Power and water availability remain critical constraints for project execution, Nomura noted. Investments in India’s information technology (IT) services sector reached 4.5 per cent of the gross domestic product (GDP) over the 12-month period from Q42025 through Q32026, according to a research note by Nomura. This marks an increase from 0.8 per cent during the same period a year earlier. New data centre projects and an upward revision in the cost of existing projects were key drivers for this rise, Nomura said. The IT sector’s share accounted for approximately 28.4 per cent of total new investment projects announced. A tax holiday for foreign companies, mentioned in Union Budget 2026-27 , also buoyed these investment announcements, Nomura reported, citing data from the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy ( CMIE ). Despite the encouraging rise in announcements, Nomura cautioned that the availability of power and water remains a key constraint for project execution. India is experiencing a structural shift, with rising services imports impacting its services trade surplus , Nomura noted. Increased imports of consultancy, digital, technical, and trade services could be attributed to the growing importance of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, and a focus on data centres, alongside rising intellectual property (IP) imports. Nomura partly attributed the rising IP imports to lower domestic research and development spending. India’s current account deficit increased by $3.5 billion year-on-year in the April-August period of FY27, despite cushioning from remittances and a services surplus. national_raw_news.title: Centre to launch nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan-Rabi 2026’ from Haryana today
national_raw_news.content: Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will launch the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan-Rabi 2026’ from Karnal in Haryana today. The campaign will continue until November 30. The initiative is aimed at promoting sustainable agriculture, improving soil health and encouraging the judicious use of agricultural resources. The campaign aims to create awareness among farmers about the balanced and judicious use of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs based on soil testing. It will promote crop diversification through oilseed, pulse and horticulture missions, encourage the effective utilisation of fallow fields after paddy harvesting and promote proper crop residue management. The campaign will also focus on training farmers in the appropriate use of organic and bio-based agricultural products and promoting natural farming through awareness programmes, training sessions and field demonstrations. As part of the campaign, farmers’ conferences, Kisan Chaupals, training sessions and field demonstrations will be organised at the state, district, block and Gram Panchayat levels. Agriculture departments, Krishi Vigyan Kendras, ICAR institutes and agricultural universities will work together to ensure wider participation to strengthen public outreach. Awareness about the campaign will also be spread through local-language information materials, Radio, Doordarshan, social media and other information, education and communication activities. Through the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, the Government seeks to strengthen soil and water conservation, promote efficient and cost-effective farming practices, improve agricultural sustainability and contribute to the long-term prosperity of farmers and the vision of Viksit Bharat.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today held bilateral talks with his Polish counterpart, Donald Tusk in New Delhi. During the talks, both the leaders reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and also exchanged views on regional and global issues of mutual interest. Addressing the joint press meet, Prime Minister Modi said that the world is undergoing a period of uncertainty and transformation and despite these challenges, India and Poland are emerging as important centres of growth, technology and innovation. He said, today, both nations have reached an agreement to deepen relations in defence, space, and nuclear energy. Mr Modi invited companies from Poland to engage in co-development and co-production with India in all these strategic sectors. The Prime Minister Tusk arrived in New Delhi last evening on a three-day visit to India. He is being accompanied by the Minister of Finance and Economy, Andrzej Domanski, and a large business delegation. This is his second visit to India in his capacity as the Prime Minister of Poland. Earlier, External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar called on Prime Minister Tusk this morning. In a social media post, Dr. Jaishankar appreciated his sharing thoughts on deepening India – Poland cooperation across a wide range of domains. The Minister said that he is looking forward to his meeting with Prime Minister Modi to advance the Strategic Partnership between the two countries. The Prime Minister of Poland visited Rajghat and paid tributes to Mahatma Gandhi. Prime Minister Tusk will also travel to Bengaluru, where he will engage with various business stakeholders, including from the IT and space sectors. The visit will provide the opportunity to further strengthen the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties. Poland is India’s largest trading and investment partner in Central and Eastern Europe.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi, Toman Kumar Win Compound Mixed Team Gold for India
national_raw_news.content: India’s para archers Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar clinched the compound mixed team gold at the Asian Para Games, beating Indonesia’s Teodora Audi Ayudia Ferelly and Ken Swagumilang 151-148 in a one-sided final in Aichi-Nagoya today. The top-seeded Indians, who set a new world record in the qualification round, consistently hit the target to build and maintain their lead throughout the clash. India edged ahead 38-37 in the opening end before extending their advantage to four points at 77-73 in the second, dropping just one point in the process. Earlier, Suvarna Raj bagged a gold medal by winning the women’s F-54 discus throw event. In para-archery, Swati Chaudhary secured silver in the women’s W-1 category. In para table tennis, Bhavina Patel and Shubham Wadhwa confirmed a medal in mixed doubles XD7 after defeating Japan’s Kimie Bessho and Masanori Uno in straight games, 11-9, 11-3, and 11-6. They will face a South Korean pair in the semifinals. Meanwhile, Dattaprasad Chougule and Savita lost 2-3 to the Philippines in the XD17 quarterfinals despite winning the first two games. India also secured several bronze medals in para-badminton. Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat lost their mixed doubles semifinal to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramadani. Sanjana Kumari won bronze in women’s singles SL3, while Suhas Yathiraj and Abhijeet Sakhuja secured bronze in men’s singles SL4. Krishna Nagar and Nithya Sre also claimed bronze in mixed doubles SH6.

national_raw_news.title: India aims one-trillion-dollar chemicals market by 2040, says Union Minister J. P. Nadda
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Chemicals and Fertilisers J. P. Nadda has said that India aims to develop a one-trillion-dollar chemicals market by 2040. Inaugurating the 14th edition of India Chem 2026 at the Bombay Exhibition Centre, NESCO, in Mumbai today, he said a favourable environment is emerging in the country for the growth of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector. He added that clear policies, government support and positive industry participation are opening up new opportunities for investment and growth in the sector. Mr. Nadda said that under the government’s proposed ‘Bhavya Rasayan’ scheme, the Centre would provide one thousand crore rupees for each chemical park, while the concerned state would have to contribute a minimum of 500 crore rupees. He said the development of world-class infrastructure, including port, rail, air and road connectivity, would be crucial to the selection and success of these parks. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the chemicals and petrochemicals sector could make a significant contribution towards achieving the goal of making Maharashtra a one-trillion-dollar economy. He added that the sector already provides employment to three lakh people in the state. Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilisers, and Health and Family Welfare, Anupriya Patel said the Central Government is committed to promoting the growth of the chemicals and petrochemicals sector through policy support, streamlined regulations and infrastructure development. Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and senior officials from the Central and state governments were also present at the event. The theme of the 14th edition of India Chem is “Advantage Bharat: An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub”. The 3- day event will conclude on Saturday.
